headline: The cost of CoreWeave's debt jumped on 14 Oct 2026, with its 2032 bond yield near 15 percent and its shares down as much as 17 percent.
score_reason: Stays at the pool score: a sharp market move at a leading AI computing company, carried by several outlets.
importance_line: Lenders and investors in AI infrastructure and companies that rent CoreWeave's chips are most affected, and it is not yet clear whether this is a one-day panic or a lasting repricing of AI debt.
summary: Business Insider reports that investors demanded almost 15 percent to hold CoreWeave's 2032 bonds, which the company sold in June at 9.625 percent, and that its shares fell as much as 17 percent to $64.41. CoreWeave rents out high-end AI chips and has more than $50 billion of debt, so the move feeds a debate over whether the borrowing behind the AI building boom is getting riskier.
notes: MarketWatch original blocked (HTTP 401); read Business Insider's report (partly behind a paywall; the opening was readable). Other outlets (CNBC, Yahoo Finance, Motley Fool, Investopedia) carry the same story by headline.
